method: After freezing the decision and canonical bytes, returned to the official 2026–2027 regulations and independently re-totalled Appendix 3. Rechecked the standard and conditional advancement rules, the separate lab attendance credit and the graduation assessment against Articles 5.2, 5.3 and 5.8–5.9. Reconsidered the current course evidence and compared it to the exact finished pair. This is a separate pass by the same AI.
findings: The 2026–2027 regulations confirm the English, full-time Maastricht BSc, 180 EC over three years. Article 3.6 and Appendix 3 give Year 1 as 41 EC of courses and 19 EC of longitudinal development, lab and design work. Year 2 is 38 EC of courses and 22 EC in the longitudinal lines, including one 7 EC design project. The first-listed Clinical Track is a neutral example and the Technological Track is an alternative. The 5 EC lab work and 2 EC attendance units appear once per year. Year 3 has a 30 EC minor followed by one 30 EC individual graduation project, including internship, thesis and oral defence. The internship and defence codes are components of that award. The minor remains open, with approval required where applicable. No mandatory named minor or additional project credit is inferred.

Article 5.3 gives unconditional progression after all 60 Year 1 credits and after the full 120 first- and second-year credits. Conditional Year 2 entry requires three of four eight-week courses, one of two four-week courses and two of three longitudinal lines with the specified lab-credit condition. Conditional Year 3 entry also requires all Year 1 credits and corresponding Year 2 course and longitudinal-line minima. The standard example completes each year before entering the next. Article 3.7 allows an approved set of electives to supplement a shorter minor to 30 EC and sets conditions for external choices. Articles 5.2, 5.8 and 5.9 set the 6.0 minimum for the internship/thesis/defence, individual writing and oral assessment by two examiners, and a supervised placement meeting programme rules.

The current regulations confirm the component set and credit allocation. The UCR plan has substantive overlap in science, laboratory work, data and design and clear gaps in specialised biomaterials, fabrication and clinical translation. The rescheduling preserves the plan. Reader-facing content distinguishes the current curriculum and required 30 EC project from optional UCR research.
